title: Marigold Payments on-prem sizing + KMS integration playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working playbook for Marigold Payments' first on-prem Redwood private deployment. The primary goals are:
- Provide a low-risk sizing and HA topology that meets Marigold's SLOs (p50 < 120ms token latency for 512 context, 99.9% availability on inference control plane).
- Document Terraform module choices, variable mappings, and state handling for the customer-managed onboarding path.
- Capture KMS/HSM integration options (Marigold requires BYOK + audit logs forwarded to their Splunk instance).
- Outline a staged upgrade plan for moving from the current 2025 infra baseline to our 2026 runtime release with minimal disruption.

High-level customer constraints / assumptions:
- Marigold network: single primary data center in FRA (AWS Outpost) with a DR site in DUB (on-prem colo).
- Compliance: PCI-DSS scoped; keys must be customer-managed. No egress of raw payment PII allowed to hosted Redwood control plane.
- Expected steady-state throughput: 200 qps (text-generation tokens) average across 3 models, with 600 qps peak during AM batch window.
- Average prompt length: 350 tokens; average generation 80 tokens. Typical sequence length distribution included in appendix.
- Budget guidance: aim for < $9k/month infra cost (customer cap for POC).
- Customer will provide L2 network, KVM access for initial hardware and an NFS-backed artifact store; Redwood will own the software stack/deployment.

Sizing recommendation (initial POC cluster):
1) Inference pool (GPU nodes):
- 4 x A100-80GB equiv (can be q8/4 quantized models) as dedicated serving nodes for model variants A/B/C.
- Each node target throughput (conservative): 160 qps for average tokens (batch size 8, concurrency 20).
- Reasoning: provides headroom for 600 qps peak when autoscaling via burst pool + warm standby.

2) Orchestration & control plane (customer-managed, small footprint):
- 3 x m5.large (or equivalent) VMs for control-plane services (API gateway, rollout controller, metrics ingester).
- Redis: 2 x r5.large cluster for ephemeral KV cache + prefix cache metadata (replicated across DNS zones).
- Postgres: 1 primary + 1 replica (db.t3.medium -> POC); use WAL shipping to DR replica.

3) Storage and artifacts:
- NFS with 2TB usable for model artifacts, container images; ensure ~2x growth buffer for model versions.
- Local NVMe scratch on GPU nodes for KV cache (recommended 1TB NVMe each).

4) Networking:
- Dual NICs on GPU hosts: mgmt + inference (segregated).
- 25 Gbps interior switch recommended for Gpu-to-gpu transfers and KV exchange during batching.

KMS/HSM integration options (customer constraint: BYOK required):
- Option A (preferred): AWS CloudHSM on Outpost with key material imported by Marigold. Redwood integrates via KMIP bridge (our control plane expects a KMS URI). This preserves key ownership; Redwood runtime uses KMS for envelope encryption of model artifacts and secrets.
- Option B: External HSM (Thales) with KMIP endpoint. Redwood will rely on TLS mutual auth + signed certs provided by Marigold. Adds latency of ~2-6ms per key op — tested in staging.
- Requirement: All key access must be logged and forwarded to Splunk via customer syslog endpoint. We will add a FluentBit sidecar on control-plane nodes to forward the KMS audit stream.

Terraform module notes (current modules + TODOs):
- Use module: modules/aws-k8s-cluster (forked from infra repo). We will add a wrapper module private-deployments/marigold-edge that sets default node pools and network mapping to their Outpost CIDR.
- State remote: Use S3 backend with customer-managed encryption (SSE-KMS) and a dedicated DynamoDB lock table. For POC, store state in a non-shared S3 bucket owned by Marigold; recommend rolling this into the customer's infra account.
- Variables mapping (important):
  - var.cluster_cidr -> DEPLOY_CIDR (mapped to Outpost network)
  - var.kms_key_arn -> marigold_kms_key_arn
  - var.model_artifact_path -> s3://marigold-redwood-models/2026-03-poC
- Outputs to capture:
  - control_plane_endpoint, model_registry_bucket, kms_binding_status
- Migration note: existing modules expect provider alias aws.primary. Marigold uses cross-account roles for DR. We need to add provider alias support to the wrapper (DONE in draft branch).
- Sensitive values: mark with sensitive=true and avoid printing in plan/apply logs. Ensure TF_LOG not set in pipelines.

Zero-downtime upgrade playbook (2026 runtime release => feature set X):
Stage 0: Preparation (2 weeks)
- Smoke tests for model outputs vs canonical eval set (baseline).
- Bake Runtime image and push to customer artifact repo (tagged).
- Create canary config: single GPU node with traffic split 5%.
- Backout plan: ability to route 100% traffic to previous runtime within 90s via rollout controller.

Stage 1: Canary (1 day)
- Deploy new runtime on canary node. Run synthetic load at 2x expected per-node throughput. Monitor latency, token-cost, and quality regressions (automated eval runs).
- Checkpoint logs and KMS audit; verify no PII leakage in logs.

Stage 2: Gradual rollout (3 days)
- 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100% traffic split with 1 hour observation at each step.
- If token-cost delta > 7% or latency p50 increased > 20ms, pause rollout and trigger rollback.

Stage 3: Post-upgrade stabilization (2 days)
- Run full regression suite, rebaseline model-profiler metrics, update Optimize suggested quant profiles if needed.

Terraform upgrade notes:
- Apply modules in this order: network -> kms -> storage -> control-plane -> serving-runtime.
- Keep Terraform state locks enabled; perform apply in maintenance window when external CI/CD agents are not running parallel applies.

Customer architecture Q&A (answered during scoping calls):
Q: Can we run the control plane in Redwood-managed SaaS but keep inference on-prem?
A: No for Marigold (policy) — all control plane components must be customer-managed for compliance. Our code supports that path but requires additional telemetry forwarding setup.

Q: Where do model artifacts live?
A: Customer preference is an S3-compatible object store on their Outpost. For the POC we will accept NFS as temporary, but final solution must be S3-compatible with versioning + lifecycle policies.

Q: What is the expected latency overhead for KMS envelope encryption?
A: Per-key op measured ~2ms (CloudHSM) to ~6ms (external HSM); envelope operations are batched and cached — amortized impact on inference path ≈ <1ms per request after caching.

Operational runbook fragments (quick checklist):
- Pre-flight: verify Outpost Windows, check NIC bonding, ensure SNMP alerts configured to customer NOC.
- On-call shift: include Redwood SRE pager for 72 hours post-upgrade, rotate names: Ethan, Priya, Lena.
- Escalation: ticket to ENG-PLATFORM channel; if KMS errors, reproduce with kms_client get-key-policy call and run kms-diagnostics.sh.

Open questions / risks:
- PCI scoping: need confirmation from Marigold's auditor whether Redwood agents reading only tokenized payloads is in-scope. (Action: POC security questionnaire -> SEC-383).
- DR failover latency: Cross-site replication for model artifacts not yet tested at required SLA. Plan a separate test to validate full failover within 5 minutes.
- Terraform drift detection: customer wants weekly drift reports — need to finalize a runbook for automated drift scans (Jira: JIRA-ENG-2191).

Action items (owners):
- Ethan: finalize the terraform wrapper module and open PR (github: infra/pull/512) — due 2026-02-22.
- Maya: run KMS latency microbenchmarks with customer HSM and populate results in confluence page (CON-1023) — due 2026-02-18.
- Priya: draft the maintenance window and rollback playbook and share with Marigold security by 2026-02-20.
- Omar: prepare synthetic load harness for canary testing and document runbook (JIRA-ENG-2191) — due 2026-03-01.

Appendix: quick cost estimate (POC monthly):
- GPUs: 4 x A100 (rental-equivalent) = $5,200/mo (est)
- Control plane VMs + DB + Redis = $850/mo
- Storage (S3 / NFS) = $550/mo
- Network egress internal = $150/mo
- Contingency + monitoring licenses = $450/mo
Total ~ $7.2k/mo (below customer cap for POC). Note: cost will rise for production-grade HA + DR.

Notes on documentation & handoffs:
- Create a README in infra repo with variables mapping and sample tfvars for Marigold account (branch marigold-onprem).
- Add a confluence quickstart with commands to rotate KMS keys and to run the canary rollback: CON-1023 (draft).

Unresolved / brainstorming fragments (kept here for context):
- Consider a lightweight gateway appliance (ARM-based) for tokenization at the edge to reduce PII exposure to runtime. Pros: reduces scoping; cons: increases latency and ops surface.
- Explore using a containerized KMIP proxy to normalize heterogeneous HSMs behind a single interface. Could simplify integration for future customers.

End of working draft.
If you edit this file, drop a note in #eng-private-deployments with a short diff summary.
